note: Ground truth via irw::irw_table_sets() (21 items, resp 1-5, 4242 rows, n=202). Code derivation (core model s3): POSITIONAL -- data/dominguez_2018_job_crafting.py assigns item_N to the Nth entry of a hard-coded column list, so the positional claim was checked rather than assumed: for all 21 items the live item x resp frequency table matches the source column's value counts cell for cell (e.g. item_10 49/84/47/16/6). Block assignment corroborated by the paper's published skill means (structural 4.505 vs 4.50, hindering 2.719 vs 2.71, social 3.862 vs 3.86; challenging 3.325 vs 3.39, low only because of the item_17 defect). DEVIATIONS from literal transcription, all deliberate: (a) item_17 ships with blank item_text and blank option_text because the source column labelled 'Item 17' holds the mean of items 18-21, not a response (see notes); (b) item 14 is shipped as 'I look to my supervisor for inspiration' -- the CC BY Table 2 reads '...for inspiration capabilities', a duplication artifact from the row above; the Tims et al. 2012 original has no 'capabilities'; (c) English wording is a substitute for the Spanish administration (deposit and paper contain no Spanish item text); (d) no instructions text exists in either source, left blank rather than invented. option_text is the deposit's own anchor legend, transcribed verbatim from S1 row 1: '1: Never, 2: Almost never, 3: Sometimes, 4: Often 5: Very often'. wording_rights=NC recorded on the arnoldbakker.com clause quoted in notes; basis is weak in one respect (the questionnaire list is login-gated so JCS coverage is inferred from the page's scope), and the table ships under the source-licence rule because the wording was copied from a CC BY 4.0 article.
public_note: item_17 carries no item text: in this study's own data file the column labelled 'Item 17' contains the mean of items 18-21 (141 of 202 values are non-integers) rather than a response, and IRW stores it truncated to an integer, so no wording can honestly be attached to it. The other 20 items are the canonical English Job Crafting Scale wording; the study administered a Spanish version whose wording is not in the deposit or the paper.
